name: Should I remove the tub if this is the only bathroom my kids use?

mainEntity.name: Should I remove the tub if this is the only bathroom my kids use?

acceptedAnswer.text: A layout can support children better by making bathing, storage, supervision, and cleaning easier. A tub may remain valuable for young children, while a handheld shower, durable surfaces, reachable hooks, rounded or protected edges, and organized storage can improve daily use. Avoid placing fragile accessories or hard-to-reach controls in the main traffic path. Explain the children’s ages, bathing habits, and whether the room must later serve adults. Elite Remodeling & Design can compare a family-focused plan with a more adult-oriented design before construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not automatically. If the bathroom is the home’s only bathing space for young children, retaining a tub may provide useful flexibility. Balance that need against shower access, floor area, storage, and future household use. A handheld shower and durable, easy-clean finishes can improve a tub-based layout.
